Furthermore, I like eating nuts as snacks as it is a healthier option. However, once in a blue moon, I allow myself to have a chocolate bar. By eating a variety of healthy foods in reasonable portions, I manage to keep a balanced diet.

questions.q: Would you participate in this activity?
questions.model: Yes, I would. The people in the picture are educating the public by distributing posters on how to fight dengue. They appear friendly with smiling faces. They are also made up of different races which shows the community spirit. I also believe they are made of different races so they can speak in different languages other than English. I believe raising awareness about dengue will help immensely. We should work together as a community to prevent illnesses like dengue from spreading. We should educate public on how to prevent dengue and what to do when we contract dengue. Also, as a citizen, we should practise social responsibility. We should follow the steps of the mozzie wipeout and do other preventive measures. Therefore, I would participate in this activity as I believe it is important to educate the public about dengue.

questions.q: What do you do at home to prevent dengue?
questions.model: There are a few other methods we can do to prevent dengue. We prevent water accumulation on the trays of the dish drying racks. We use insecticide sprays in dark corners like under the bed or burn repellent oils inside our home. Also, we made ourselves aware of the dengue colour-coded alert system so we can protect our family. The system uses colour coded banners – yellow, red or green) Red means there are more than 10 cases, yellow means there are less than 10 cases and green means we should remain vigilant. For example, when our neighbourhood colour code turned to yellow, my parents installed mosquito screens on our windows and doors. Also, I had to sleep under a mosquito net. On top of that, I helped by clearing the water from the vases. I did this every 2 to 3 days. Luckily, the code eventually turned to green, but we continued staying vigilant. These are some ways we prevent dengue at home.

questions.q: Do you think it is important for schools to educate students about how to prevent dengue?
questions.model: It’s important to start early in educating the public. I believe we should start with schools. Educating students help build awareness, ensuring students grow up with habits that protect public health. For example, we had a school talk on “Mozzie Wipeout”, a public health initiative aimed at preventing the spread of dengue. The host shared to us practical steps on how we can prevent dengue at home. It involved steps like, emptying and cleaning containers that collect water, covering water storage to prevent mosquito access and using mosquito repellents and nets to avoid bites. These steps were easy fore me to share with family and friends. Therefore, it is important to instil these habits early.

questions.q: What are the people in the photograph doing? Do you think it is effective?
questions.model: The people in the photograph appear to be part of a campaign that raises awareness about dengue. The people in the posters are wearing backpack billboards. I believe many of them are volunteers as some of them are wearing shirts which read, ‘Volunteer Corps’. The billboard shows steps on how to stop dengue. They also seem to be engaging with people at a hawker centre to raise awareness. I believe human billboards are effective compared to stagnant advertising mainly because they move around. The human element is important because they can directly answer any questions or queries. Also their uniqueness catches attention from the public. Therefore, I think their campaign to raise awareness about dengue is effective.

questions.q: Do you think that the poster is effective in preventing dengue?
questions.model: Yes, it is effective. The poster uses acronyms like B.L.O.C.K and S.A.W to simplify the message. It also show clear steps using pictures to educate citizens on what steps to take. The poster is not too colourful and only uses the colours red and grey. The picture of the big mosquito at the top clearly tells citizens what the campaign is about. Acronyms are effective because it is easy for citizens to remember the message. The acronyms in this poster capture attention quickly and spread awareness by encouraging clear actions on how to block mosquitoes from spreading or how to prevent bites. The uses of red against grey makes citizens focus on the important steps to take. The big picture of the mosquito is useful to convey that this is a campaign about dengue. Hence, I believe it is an effective poster in preventing dengue.

questions.q: What are some suggestions you have to educate people to become responsible citizens?
questions.model: I have two suggestions which my family practices as well. My family sprays insecticide on dark corners of our home. For example, under the bed and behind the sofa. We also have installed mosquito screens on our windows and doors. We also alert neighbours if we find dengue breeding spots. For example, we spray insecticide weekly. On top of that, my mother encourages our neighbours to do the same. She even bought a few bottles for our neighbours. By taking care of our own households and encouraging our neighbours, we can become responsible citizens and protect against dengue. Describe details from the picture to explain how effective it is!

Also, it is indicated as a ‘new virus.’ The cases may have been increasing and therefore the teacher must have been instructed to give the talk to raise awareness.

questions.q: How has Covid-19 affected your life?
questions.model: It has affected me negatively and positively. Being someone who loves going outdoors, the circuit-breaker was a challenge. I had to stay indoors, and I really missed the outdoors. Also, I had to celebrate my birthday during the lockdown. My friends and relatives attended my party via Zoom and Skype. However, it has also helped us as a family to bond closer together. For example, my parents work long hours, and they hardly have time to spend with me. During the lockdown, we bonded over board games, shows and found creative ways to entertain each other. My father edited my birthday party video with Disney princesses. So, it looks like the princesses attended my party. I was touched by his gesture. Therefore, Covid-19 has both been a boon and a bane in my life.

questions.q: Do you think your school was successful in stopping the spread of Covid-19?
questions.model: Yes, my school was successful in stopping the spread of Covid-19. During the pandemic, my school switched to Home-Based Learning until the virus was under control. Covid-19 spreads quickly in groups especially when they are in proximity. Thanks to technology, we can have lessons from home. I think my school took this to their advantage and kept students safely at home. Some other measures they did was to practise social distancing. Our desks were placed far apart from each other. Also, they ensured we took our temperatures often. This helped monitor who had the virus and who did not. My school also made wearing masks mandatory. Finally, they educated us on how to wash our hands. They also distributed hand sanitisers and encouraged the usage of it. I believe all these steps helped in stopping the spread of Covid-19.

questions.q: Are you like the boy in this picture? Do you prefer processed foods as snacks?
questions.model: Yes and no. The boy seem to be enjoying junk food. I believe he is eating potato fries. He appears to be enjoying his snack. Mostly, I prefer healthy snacks like fruits and nuts. But sometimes, I allow myself to enjoy like the boy in the picture. My favourite processed snacks are potato chips. However, I am aware that it is high in sugar, salt and fat which is not good for the long term. Therefore, I mostly steer clear from it. However, once in a while, I do indulge a little which I believe is okay. I also hope the boy in the picture is not doing this everyday. Processed foods can be dangerous if taken excessively. Currently, Singapore ranks third globally for kidney disease and this disease usually occurs due to the intake of processed foods. Therefore, I only indulge sometimes and not all the time as I am aware of the dangers of processed foods.

questions.q: How do you maintain a healthy lifestyle?
questions.model: My mother helps me maintain a healthy lifestyle. She teaches me about healthy food habits. Therefore, I ensure I eat a balanced diet with a variety of vegetables and fruits. I also exercise regularly. For example, my mother ensures I get different types of vegetables every day. She feels if I eat a variety, I can get sufficient vitamins and minerals. When I am at school, I choose brown rice over white rice. I also ensure I have vegetables. Additionally, I avoid fried foods and choose steamed foods instead. Every day, I play badminton with my friends. This gives me adequate exercise. I also choose my snacks wisely. I stay away from anything that has too much salt or sugar. Lastly, I make it a point to stay hydrated. My mother bought me a cute water bottle that has markers with encouraging messages on it. This motivates me to drink up. Most importantly, my mother chooses to stock our pantry with healthy snacks! By eating healthily, exercising regularly, making healthier choices and drinking adequate amounts of water, I maintain a healthy lifestyle.

questions.q: Do you have suggestions on what type of snacks children your age should eat?
questions.model: I suggest fruit juices and nuts. I enjoy eating nuts a lot. Pistachios are my favourite type of nuts. They are an excellent source of fats, fibre, and zinc. I particularly like them because I heard they are good for the brain. Apart from pistachios, I enjoy chestnuts. They contain many vitamins and minerals too. As for fruit, I like oranges. They are rich in vitamin C and is refreshing on a hot day. For example, whenever I am low on energy, I eat pistachios. I find them convenient. I do not have to cook them. It is also a great source of energy. I love eating chestnuts with a little bit of salt. My aunt prepares them that way during teatime. It is a great source of energy! As for oranges, my favourite way of preparing them is to make fresh orange juice. Compared to popcorn and sandwiches, I feel more satiated when I eat fruit and nuts. These are the suggestions I have for healthy snacks.

questions.q: How do you think the little girl in the picture is feeling?

questions.q: Do you think it is important for children to learn how to cook healthy?
questions.model: It is important for children to learn how to cook healthy food as it promotes long-term health and well-being. When children learn how to prepare nutritious meals, they develop an understanding of what foods contribute to a balanced diet and how to make healthier food choices. This can help prevent chronic health issues like obesity, heart disease, and diabetes later in life. Children who are involved in cooking and meal preparation are more likely to make healthier food choices, both in childhood and into adulthood. My mother involves me in cooking. I accompany her to buy groceries for special occasions. She also teaches me to cook basic recipes like soups, sandwiches and pasta. She also tells me what each ingredient does for the body. Eventually, I would need to cook when I am an adult so it is important to learn how to cook or we can end up eating processed foods which can be harmful for the body. In my opinion, I think it is important parents teach children how to cook healthy meals.

questions.q: Are you influenced by what your family and friends eat?
questions.model: Yes, I am influenced by what my family and friends eat. I once read that you are the average of the five people you surround yourself with. The people who you are closest to will influence the way you eat. I am fortunate that my family eats very healthy. However, my friends not so much. For example, my parents are very particular that I eat a variety of vegetables. They also stock the pantry with healthy snacks like dried fruits and nuts. Whenever, I am at home, I eat healthily. However, when I am out with my friends, we frequent fast food joints. Since we are students, fast food is the cheapest option for us. To accommodate my friends, I do indulge in fast food whenever I am out with them. So yes, I am definitely influenced by what my friends and family eat. When we are sick, it is important to wear a mask so we do not spread our infection to others. I think it is a powerful message that the prime minister is sending out to residents.

questions.q: Do you think being socially responsible is important?
questions.model: I believe social responsibility is the key to preventing the spread of infectious diseases. If everyone follows the mandatory guidelines given by the Ministry of Health, together as a community, we can prevent the spread of such diseases. For example, some people were resistant to wearing masks in public despite knowing that Covid 19 spreads through droplets transmitted from an infected person. Also, there were cases, where quarantined persons left the home before the quarantine period was over, endangering the public. This type of social irresponsibility can make it hard to stop the spread. If more and more people do not cooperate, it becomes harder to stop the spread of such infectious diseases. We have a responsibility towards our society. We should not endanger the lives of others. Therefore, I believe social responsibility is the key to stopping the spread of infectious diseases and other issues in society.

questions.q: In what ways have you been socially responsible?
questions.model: During covid, I was socially responsible by following health guidelines. I had worn masks in public, got myself vaccinated and I carried a hand sanitiser with me at all times. I also did not flout any rules set by the government like going out when I am not allowed to. Apart from covid, there are other examples of social responsibility that I have done. For example, I return trays at hawker centres. I also did the Mozzie Wipeout, which was a campaign to prevent the spread of dengue. I have also taken part in recycling campaigns. These are some ways I have been socially responsible.
